stemMd: A solid cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 8 cm. A cylindrical hole of radius 1 cm is drilled along its axis through the entire height. What volume of solid remains?
explanationMd: Subtract the removed cylindrical volume from the original volume. Both cylinders have height 8 cm, so the remaining volume is π(3² − 1²) × 8 = π(9 − 1) × 8 = 64π cm³. The result is less than the original 72π cm³ by exactly the removed 8π cm³.

distractorRationale.e: This is the original cylinder volume before removing the hole.
distractorRationale.b: This is the volume removed, not the volume remaining.
distractorRationale.c: This squares the difference of radii, giving π(3−1)² × 8, instead of subtracting their squared radii.
distractorRationale.d: This adds the removed volume to the original instead of subtracting it.
